agree.reason: A Ridgeview retiree who voted no last time hears that their own branch closes in July and gets a plain $10-a-month figure they can check, which could move some resisters, though the card gives no reason the levy was redesigned since the last one failed.

honest.reason: Every number traces to the brief and the misleading coffee line was dropped, but 'pays for exactly two things' and 'tightly limited' go slightly further than the brief, which doesn't say the money is legally restricted to those uses.

works_the_facts.reason: The $122 a year and $10 a month figures come correctly from 19 cents × $640,000 and suit the precinct, and the card gives a formula for working out your own bill; a per-day figure or the city-median comparison could have made it look smaller and still be true.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is put concretely: the Ridgeview branch closes this July and Sunday hours stay gone, set against the 22% rise in visits.

qualification.reason: A door script stating fixed terms needs no hedge, and the card adds none.

objections.reason: It answers the 'blank check' letter with the fixed rate, the six-year limit and the named uses, and treats the fixed-income worry with respect, without bringing up objections the reader didn't have.

fit.reason: The main pitch fits on one side of a card and runs about 60 to 90 seconds with short rebuttals underneath; it leaves out the requested coffee line, which is defensible because the claim isn't true for Ridgeview homes.
